question: Why did Bach, in a 1730 letter to an old school friend, count a healthy year in Leipzig as a loss?
answer: Because part of his pay came from funerals. Writing to Georg Erdmann, he valued his post at about 700 thalers a year, part of it fees for burials and weddings, and complained that when a healthy wind blew, deaths fell and his income with them. He was asking Erdmann for a post elsewhere.
move: Look at how a job is paid before judging what the worker hopes for.
reference: Neumann and Schulze (eds), Bach-Dokumente, vol. 1, Bärenreiter, 1963, letter of 28 October 1730
